what.text: This page follows refugees from the Central African Republic living in the Republic of the Congo, as counted by UNHCR at the end of each year.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 30252 Central African refugees there, 4.5% of all refugees from the Central African Republic.
Cameroon, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Chad host more of them than the Republic of the Congo does.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflict over the government of the Central African Republic in several periods from 2001, with Seleka and anti-Balaka among the opponents from 2009 to 2014.
From 2017 to 2025 the opponents it records include anti-Balaka, UPC, CPC and CMSPR.

when.text: UNHCR's series for this group starts in 1986 at 230 refugees.
The main years of displacement in the data are 2014 to 2018 and 2020 to 2025, and the figure is at its highest at the end of 2025.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took or where they live in the Republic of the Congo.
These are year-end totals for the Republic of the Congo only, reported to UNHCR.
